newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday December 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday December 19.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi asks the ruling coalition for other "signs of change", but seems ready to strike a deal over the set up of an all-party commission to carry out constitutional reforms. The upper house Senate is due to vote on the proposal on January 15 (all).
* After four confidence votes called by the government in three days, the upper house Senate approved the 1997 austerity budget (all).
* A law proposal is under examination in Parliament which would ease sanctions for illicit parties' financing (all).

* Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti says there might be a general debate on the welfare state and does not rule out the possibility to intervene on "baby-pensions", which are attributed after a working period of 19 years and 6 months (all).

* European Commissioner Karel Van Miert criticised Italy's government saying he should have been informed of the 1.977 trillion lire capital increase kicked off by the Treasury for ailing Banco di Napoli (all).

* Boards from the Treasury-controlled Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) and Mediocredito Centrale are expected to approve two rival bids for a 60 percent stake in Banco di Napoli. BNL is joining forces with insurer INA (all).
* Talks are due to resume today between the employers association Confindustria and trade unions over the renewal of metalworkers contract (all).
* October producer prices rose 0.4 percent on a annual basis. December preliminary CPI inflation from first group of Italian sample cities is released today (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
